units.source_text: 往日，我在舞鹤，总觉得金阁在京都一角上，是永恒的存在。

en.t: In the old days, when I was in Maizuru, I always felt that the Golden Pavilion, standing in one corner of Kyoto, was an eternal presence.

units.source_text: 可是，一旦住在这里，金阁就只在我眺望的时候才会出现在我的眼前。

en.t: But once I came to live here, the Golden Pavilion appeared before my eyes only when I gazed at it.

units.source_text: 晚上睡在大雄宝殿时，我觉得金阁似乎不存在。

en.t: At night, when I slept in the main hall, I felt as though the Golden Pavilion did not exist.

units.source_text: 所以我每天无数次地去眺望金阁，遭到了师兄弟的耻笑。

en.t: So every day I went countless times to gaze at the Golden Pavilion, and was mocked by my fellow acolytes.

units.source_text: 不论看多少遍，我都觉得那里存在金阁简直是不可思议的。

en.t: No matter how many times I looked, I felt it was simply incredible that the Golden Pavilion existed there.

units.source_text: 于是，眺望过后，我折回大雄宝殿的当儿，

en.t: And so, after gazing at it, just as I was turning back toward the main hall,

units.source_text: 如果猛然回头再望望，就会觉得金阁恍如欧里秋克①顿时消逝，无影无踪了。

en.t: if I suddenly looked back once more, I would feel that the Golden Pavilion, like Eurydice, had vanished in an instant without a trace.
